newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ bill yields close 9 pts lower on soaring Kiwi.
newsitem.headline: NZ bill yields close 9 pts lower on soaring Kiwi.

text.p: 0500 GMT
* Soaring currency sees 90-day bank bill yields fall 9 pts
* Bond yields end little changed
* Market seen running out of steam
* Cash at 10.00 pct vs 10.00 pct at Tuesday's close
* 90 day bills 9.80 pct vs 9.89 pct
* 7/98 bond yields 8.13 pct vs 8.14 pct
* 02/01 bond yields 8.35 pct vs 8.35 pct
* 11/06 bond yields 8.40 pct vs 8.38 pct
* Dec bank bill futures 90.72 vs 90.63, vol 2,357
New Zealand bank bill yields rallied nearly 10 points on Wednesday mainly in response to a soaring New Zealand dollar, which hit an eight-year high.
The December bill futures rose nine points to 90.72 on volume of 2,357.
Almost the sole impetus was the sharp rise of the currency with both the spot rate and Trade-Weighted Index rising to their highest levels since June 1988 -- to 70 U.S. cents and 66.74 respectively.
There was also some stop-loss buying as shorts from Tuesday regrouped.

However, dealers said the market was starting to run out of steam. They said the 90-day bills were in a 10.00-9.75 percent range and the Reserve Bank had made it clear last week it did not want bills too far below 10 percent.
There was interest in the short-dated bonds with more rumours of further dual currency issues. The 7/98 bonds ended one point lower at 8.13 percent.
Longer bonds ended a couple of points higher but did not rise as sharply as U.S. treasuries overnight.
One bond dealer said many traders' positions were essentially set ahead of the October 12 election. She said the market was flow driven and volumes were relatively light.
-- Wellington newsroom 64 4 4734 746
